note: Hebrew wayyomer is a simple narrative past; the KJV pluperfect places the call back in Ur (harmonising with 15:7 and Acts 7:2), which the Hebrew does not mark.

mine: whoever treats you with contempt I will curse
note: Two different verbs: meqallelkha (qillel, "make light of, disdain") and 'a'or ('arar, "curse"); the KJV levels them into one, losing the contrast between human contempt and divine curse.
Hebrew 'elon is a large tree (oak or terebinth), often a sacred landmark; "plain" follows the Targum and Vulgate.
Hebrew hannegbah names the Negev, the dry region in southern Canaan; "south" hides that it is a specific region.

kjv: so I might have taken her to me to wife
mine: so that I took her as my wife
note: Hebrew wa'eqqah 'otah li le'ishah is a past consecutive: Pharaoh did take her; the KJV's "might have" suggests it was only a possibility.
